title: Visual QA pipeline — automated screenshot review for UI tasks
description:
Build a true visual QA pipeline for Mission Control. This is the #1 priority.

## What It Does
1. When a build completes on any UI task (tags: ui, frontend, component, page), auto-capture a screenshot of the affected page(s)
2. Store before/after screenshots in the task's attachments
3. A QA reviewer agent loads both screenshots, reviews the code diff, and checks:
   - Does the visual output match what the task asked for?
   - Any layout regressions? Broken elements? Overlapping text?
   - Does it look good on the dark theme?
4. If QA passes → mark task as review-approved, move to Done
5. If QA fails → add failure notes, move back to in-progress for the builder to fix

## Implementation
- Use Playwright or Puppeteer to capture screenshots (headless Chrome)
- Screenshot endpoint: POST /api/tasks/[id]/screenshot with target URL
- Store captures in task.visualReview.captures array (schema already exists)
- QA agent uses image analysis to compare before/after
- Wire into the existing build-queue pipeline: build completes → trigger visual QA → then code review

## Key Files
- src/lib/build-queue.ts — where builds complete, hook in here
- src/app/api/tasks/route.ts — task CRUD
- TaskCard already has visual QC chip rendering (visualReview field)

## Success Criteria
- Every UI task gets auto-screenshotted after build
- QA agent reviews screenshot + code before anything hits Done
- Visual regressions get caught and sent back to builder
- No human QA needed for routine UI tasks
